summary: kafka-helmsman 99.0.1 exfiltrates host identifiers at install time to OAST collectors
details: setup.py starts a module-level daemon thread on build/install that collects installer host identifiers (hostname, current working directory, platform, timestamp) and sends them to third-party out-of-band collectors: an HTTPS GET with base64-encoded data in the path to a subdomain of oast.live, a JSON POST to a webhook.site collector URL, and DNS lookups against the same oast.live domain. The beacon runs unconditionally on every pip install with no consent prompt or opt-out. The package name and version 99.0.1 target the unpublished internal name 'kafka-helmsman' (referencing github.com/teslamotors/kafka-helmsman) using the high-version shadowing pattern typical of dependency-confusion attacks, so the exfiltration primarily fires inside environments whose internal resolvers misroute the name to public PyPI. A README framing this as 'security research' does not change the data flow: installer-side host identifiers leave the machine to attacker-chosen OOB infrastructure on install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
